text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovakia's sole oil refiner Slovnaft said the strengthening dollar has been increasing its costs for the purchase of oil. Slovnaft said every dollar's increase by one Slovak crown was boosting its expenditures for oil purchases by 60 million crowns a month.

- Major Slovak producer of penicillin-based drugs, Biotika, said it expected a full year loss of around 50 million crowns mainly due to a rapid decline in prices of penicillin substances on world markets.

- Slovakia's largest pulp and paper producer, SCP Ruzomberok, expects to complete in the near future a 1.6 billion-crown system for production of eletrical energy which should cover the company's entire energy consumption.

SME - Lawyers said only a law court can declare illegal the contract between the National Property Fund (NPF) and a little-known company Druha Obchodna on privatisation of oil and gas storage company Nafta Gbely. Opposition parties have said they will seek a return of Nafta shares to the NPF if they win next year's elections.

- Opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) and the coalition of ethnic Hungarian parties said they supported attempts by other opposition parties to call an extraordinary parliamentary session to demand the return of the parliamentary mandate to Jozef Gaulieder, expelled from parliament in December.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Slovak food producing industry continued to stagnate last year. Only four sectors of the industry -- food oils, sugar production, production of pasta food and beer prodction -- last year recorded an increase, or at least maintained their prodction, against the year 1989.

- The Slovak ministry of agriculture has rejected criticism by the ministry of enviroment over the planned dam Tichy Potok in eastern Slovakia. The ministry of agriculture said the controversial dam will ensure water resources for eastern Slovakia, but final approval of the project has yet to be given by the government.
